notable_absence.finding: The page documents a request-queue-full condition without naming the setting that governs the queue depth, and without saying whether the caller should retry. Contrast extimeout.md, where the error object carries an explicit "retry": true - the field is absent here, so the reader cannot tell whether a 503 on a full queue is retryable, which is the only question a client author has. The Query Service's queue-related node-level settings are reachable via /admin/settings (see intro.md) but nothing connects them to this failure. Also absent: any error code at all - the code field is the literal placeholder <int>, so the error cannot be looked up in the error-code reference even in principle.

cross_component_finding:
This page is materially stale and malformed, and the evidence is internal. Three independent signals, all visible in the response block:

(1) Broken escaping from the AsciiDoc-to-Markdown conversion: the response opens with "     $lt; HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable" - $lt; is a mangled <, i.e. curl's "<" response-line marker. The block also ends with a stray shell prompt "$". The block is tagged as a `console` fence and hand-indented, unlike every other example in the directory, which use clean `json` fences.

(2) The error code is unresolved: "code": <int> is a placeholder that was never filled in, whereas every other error example in the batch gives a real code (1050, 1080, 3000, 12003).

(3) The metrics field set does not match any other example in the directory. This page reports mutationCount and warningCount, which no other example in the batch reports, and omits serviceLoad, which every other example in the batch reports. serviceLoad is the newer field. So this response was captured from a materially older build than its ten siblings and has not been regenerated since serviceLoad was added to the metrics object.

That third point is the useful one for this wave: the metrics field set functions as an undeclared version fingerprint on captured API output. Ten examples in this directory carry serviceLoad and one does not. There is no vocabulary in the registry for "this documented example output predates a field that now always appears", and no availableSince can be sourced for serviceLoad from any page in the batch. If reconciliation wants to track example-output staleness systematically, the shape needed is something like exampleOutputPredatesField, keyed on the response field. Recording it here because the batch's remit is version vocabulary and this is a version fact the docs express only accidentally.

This is also the only page in the batch that authenticates with no credentials at all - the curl has no -u flag and queries an unqualified keyspace "tweets" that is not part of travel-sample, further confirming it predates the other examples.
version_finding: No explicit version or edition marker on the page. Implicit version evidence only, from the metrics field set and the pre-collections keyspace name "tweets" (unqualified, i.e. bucket-only addressing rather than the bucket.scope.collection form used by every other example in the directory) - both indicating the example was captured before Couchbase Server 7.0 introduced scopes and collections and has not been refreshed since. Since the surrounding pages all use `travel-sample`.inventory.hotel, this page's addressing style is a genuine anachronism within an 8.0 documentation set rather than a deliberate simplification.
